covers: INT 1Ah, the time and date BIOS and the PCI BIOS: every function and subfunction the emulator's INT1A_Handler has a case for.

entries.name: get system time
entries.description: Returns the timer tick count since midnight and the midnight flag.
entries.behaviour: CX:DX = the tick count at 0040:006C, AL = the midnight flag at 0040:0070, which the call then clears; CF is not touched. IF is set on return. PC-98 machines install a separate INT 1Ah handler instead of this one.

sources.cites: INT 1A - TIME - GET SYSTEM TIME
case 0x00:  /* Get System time */

entries.name: set system time
entries.description: Sets the timer tick count since midnight.
entries.behaviour: CX:DX is stored as the tick count at 0040:006C. The midnight flag at 0040:0070 is left as it is. No register is returned.
entries.differs: The list says the call resets the midnight-passed flag; the emulator does not touch it.

case 0x01:  /* Set System time */

entries.name: get rtc time
entries.description: Reads the time from the real-time clock.
entries.behaviour: First sets the CMOS clock to BCD and 24-hour mode. Then CH = hours (CMOS 04h), CL = minutes (02h), DH = seconds (00h), DL = bit 0 of CMOS register 0Bh (daylight saving, set by that first step), and CF is cleared; it waits for any clock update to finish and lets the CPU idle four times.
entries.differs: The list sets CF on error (clock stopped or mid-update); the emulator always clears CF.

sources.cites: INT 1A - TIME - GET REAL-TIME CLOCK TIME (AT,XT286,PS)
case 0x02:  /* GET REAL-TIME CLOCK TIME (AT,XT286,PS) */

entries.name: set rtc time
entries.description: Sets the time of the real-time clock.
entries.behaviour: First sets the CMOS clock to BCD and 24-hour mode, waits for any update, stops updates, and writes CH, CL and DH as hours, minutes and seconds (CMOS 04h, 02h, 00h) unchanged. It sets the daylight saving bit from bit 0 of DH, then resumes updates and idles the CPU four times. CF and AH are not set.
entries.differs: The list takes the daylight saving flag from DL; the emulator takes it from bit 0 of DH, the seconds, and ignores DL.

entries.name: get rtc date
entries.description: Reads the date from the real-time clock.
entries.behaviour: First sets the CMOS clock to BCD and 24-hour mode. Then CH = century (CMOS 32h), CL = year (09h), DH = month (08h), DL = day (07h), and CF is cleared; it waits for any clock update to finish and lets the CPU idle four times.
entries.differs: The list sets CF on error; the emulator always clears CF.

case 0x04:  /* GET REAL-TIME ClOCK DATE  (AT,XT286,PS) */

entries.name: set rtc date
entries.description: Sets the date of the real-time clock.
entries.behaviour: First sets the CMOS clock to BCD and 24-hour mode, waits for any update, stops updates, and writes CH, CL, DH and DL as century, year, month and day (CMOS 32h, 09h, 08h, 07h) unchanged and unchecked. It then resumes updates and idles the CPU four times. CF and AH are not set.

entries.name: sound multiplexer
entries.description: Sets up the sound multiplexer on a PCjr or Tandy (AL = source).
entries.behaviour: On every machine type the emulator only logs an error line naming AL (the source) and returns with the registers and CF unchanged.

entries.name: tandy sound check
entries.description: Tandy digital sound installation check: returns the sound port and whether it is busy.
entries.behaviour: Acts only when the BIOS set up the Tandy DAC with a Sound Blaster or Tandy sound device; otherwise it returns at once with registers unchanged. AX = the Tandy DAC's port when that device is present, else 00C4h (the value the list gives for a Tandy 1000SL/TL). CF = set if a transfer is in progress.

entries.name: tandy sound record
entries.description: Starts recording digital sound into the buffer at ES:BX.
entries.behaviour: Needs the Tandy DAC setup as for AH=81h. CX = length, DX = delay (low 12 bits), AL = volume (low 3 bits). If a transfer is running it returns AH=00h with CF set; otherwise it starts a DMA recording, a transfer crossing a 64K page limited to the page and chained on, and returns AH=00h, CF clear.

entries.name: tandy sound stop
entries.description: Stops digital sound playback.
entries.behaviour: Needs the Tandy DAC setup as for AH=81h. It replaces the transfer with a short buffer of silence in the BIOS area at F000:A084, and returns AH=00h with CF clear.

entries.name: tandy sound reset
entries.description: Resets the Tandy digital sound hardware.
entries.behaviour: Needs the Tandy DAC setup as for AH=81h. With a Tandy DAC device it clears the low five bits of the DAC's control port; with only a Sound Blaster it writes nothing. It returns AH=00h with CF clear.

entries.name: pci bios
entries.description: The PCI BIOS entry: AL selects the function.
entries.behaviour: Active only when the PCI bus is enabled (pcibus_enable); otherwise it sets CF and leaves AH. Each call is logged at warning level. An AL that is not 01h to 03h or 08h to 0Dh is logged as an error and sets CF with AH unchanged.

sources.cites: case 0xb1:      /* PCI Bios Calls */

entries.name: pci installation
entries.description: Checks that the PCI BIOS is present and returns its version and entry point.
entries.behaviour: If the PCI bus is initialised: AH=00h, AL=01h (configuration mechanism 1), BX=0210h, CX=0000h (one bus), EDX=20494350h and EDI = the protected-mode entry point, with CF clear. Otherwise CF is set and AH is not written.

entries.name: pci find device
entries.description: Finds the SI-th PCI device with the given vendor and device ID.
entries.behaviour: CX = device ID, DX = vendor ID, SI = index. It scans the configuration space of bus 0 only; on a match AH=00h, BH=00h, BL = device and function, CF clear. With no match AH=86h and CF set.

entries.name: pci read config byte
entries.description: Reads one byte of a device's PCI configuration space.
entries.behaviour: BX = bus and device/function, DI = register. CL = the byte read, AH=00h, CF clear. It never fails: there is no register range or device existence check, and DI is masked to the register.
entries.differs: The list returns AH=87h for a bad register number; the emulator never does.
